title: ～てばかりいる — “do nothing but ～”
summary: Verb te-form + ばかりいる means the same action goes on and on, “doing nothing but ～ / always ～ing.” It often expresses the speaker's criticism or worry about the person. The action is done again and again.

patterns.form: 動詞て形 ＋ ばかりいる
patterns.gloss: te-form + ばかりいる (遊んでばかりいる, 泣いてばかりいる)

patterns.form: 動詞て形 ＋ ばかりいると、〜
patterns.gloss: …ばかりいると = if you keep doing nothing but ～, then ～

body.p: ばかり means “only, nothing but.” After a te-form it says that one action fills the person's time. Whether the action is ongoing or habitual depends on the sentence: 一日中遊んでばかりいる.
It usually shows disapproval, worry, or a complaint, such as about a child who only plays or only cries. For a neutral statement, 遊んでいる is enough.
いる can change to the past (泣いてばかりいた) or the conditional (ばかりいると). With nouns, ばかり works as in ゲームばかりしている. The meaning is about the same.

examples.ja: 弟（おとうと）は一日中（いちにちじゅう）遊（あそ）んでばかりいる。
examples.romaji: Otōto wa ichinichijū asonde bakari iru.
examples.tr: My little brother does nothing but play all day.

examples.ja: 妹（いもうと）は朝（あさ）から泣（な）いてばかりいる。
examples.romaji: Imōto wa asa kara naite bakari iru.
examples.tr: My little sister has done nothing but cry since morning.

examples.ja: ゲームをしてばかりいると、目（め）が悪（わる）くなるよ。
examples.romaji: Gēmu o shite bakari iru to, me ga waruku naru yo.
examples.tr: If you do nothing but play games, your eyesight will get worse.

pitfalls: It is te-form + ばかりいる, with the ばかり right after て. Do not add に: 遊んでばかりに is wrong.
Use it for repeated actions. A single, one-time action does not fit.
